title: Such a great trip- let me know if you want individual video reviews f...
transcript: Let's talk about all of the shows I saw in London. First I saw the Oresteia at the Bridge Theatre. This is an adaptation of a Greek trilogy of plays that has been modernized and directed by Simon Stone. This is a nearly four hour long play, but it flies by like I was locked in. I can't really speak to its merits as an adaptation, but as a play in its own right I was really impressed by it. Next I saw Death Note, based on the anime of the same name. I've been obsessed with this concept album since it came out about a decade ago, and so to finally see it get a full, lavish production was really special. The book is definitely messy as it tries to cram this entire anime into a two and a half hour show, but the really stellar performances, production design and songs really won me over. Next I saw pride at the National Theatre. This is the hot new musical in London that a lot of people are projecting will win Best Musical at the Oliviers. I found myself incredibly moved by it, although I did find the score to be a bit forgettable. But I still really enjoyed it and the ending had me sobbing. Next I saw Cyrano starring Adrian Lester. This is a pretty conventional take on the story, but it's executed really well. It's definitely a little bit longer than it needs to be, but Adrian Lester's central performance alone makes it worth seeing, and I definitely wouldn't be surprised to see him or the play in conversation when it comes to the Oliviers this spring. Next I saw Jesus Christ Superstar at the London Palladium. Now, I don't have a program for this one, but I was doing the on stage standing for the show, and that was just a really cool experience. I think I might do a full video on what that experience was like, but I will say, while I'm still not a huge fan of the show itself, I would not have wanted to watch it any other way. You really do feel like you're part of the action in a way that I have never experienced in a theatre before. Next I saw midnight at the Never Get starring Ben Platt. This one is really interesting because it's essentially a bio jukebox musical if the composer it's about was made up. And while I was not initially sold on that concept, I ended up really loving the show. I thought it was unexpectedly moving. Ben Platt is really stellar in it, and there are quite a few surprises that I won't spoil, but I thought worked very well. And the final show of my trip was Paddington. Now, I did not think that I was going to get to see Paddington this trip. I was supposed to be at the first preview of Kimberley Akimbo, but that got cancelled. And so, after refreshing the page for last minute tickets, I got my ticket about an hour before showtime. And I am so glad I did because of what a charming musical this is. It feels like so long since we've gotten a truly great show for families, but Paddington is truly a show that can be enjoyed by all ages. The music slaps. They spared no expense with the budget. And seeing it in London felt extra special because the show has so many nods to London, and the specific theatre where it is playing. And I feel like those references are going to be lost in the Broadway transfer, but it is still an excellent show that definitely lives up to the hype.
showTitle: Multiple London shows (Oresteia, Death Note, Pride, Cyrano)
classificationReason: Creator recaps 4+ London shows seen on a trip with brief opinions on each. No single-show focus. The title explicitly offers individual video reviews as separate future content, confirming this is a roundup.
